saved_responses.#49:
Definitely but any more recent examples? Lots of good work on FL hurricanes (see Sue Ann Bell's work), PR, CA wildfires…

Could use nursing home examples, too - some ghastly FL examples

Beyond the risks of acute isolation, recent research has demonstrated that a “silent” mortality among older adults follows disasters, with official death tolls significantly underestimating the impact of disasters on the elderly. Many older adults experience mortality months afterwards, due to disruptions in care and the stress of isolation. Following Hurricane Harvey, analysis reveals mortality increased among older adults with chronic health conditions which require ongoing care (e.g., chronic kidney disease (CKD) and Alzheimer’s Disease and Related Dementias (ADRD).

wildfires create a "cascading" disaster for older adults. impact is not just about the flames; it is about the intersection of chronic health conditions and the severing of social lifelines.

Building upon the evidence of post-disaster mortality among older adults, it is import to examine the factors that drive these outcomes.
